purpose: Ultra-global research registry for high-fidelity video restoration, temporal super-resolution, frame interpolation, deblurring, denoising and extreme-resolution delivery. The target is 36K/48K-class output where technically and evidentially justified, without treating invented detail as historical truth.

qualityTarget.engineeringMeaning: Extreme-resolution delivery target, not a claim that 36K or 48K factual detail can be recovered from a lower-resolution source.
qualityTarget.coreRule: Output dimensions may be increased only as far as faithful evidence and compute permit; missing information must not be presented as recovered fact.
qualityTarget.referenceReality: Current research found strong arbitrary-resolution/high-resolution video restoration systems, but no verified open-source system in this search that establishes faithful 36K or 48K video super-resolution as a standard production capability.

newCandidates.name: SeedVR2
newCandidates.notes: ICLR 2026 one-step diffusion-transformer video restoration; adaptive window attention is designed for high-resolution restoration and the official repository states restoration at any resolution. Official inference documents large-GPU requirements, so 36K/48K must be treated as a distributed/tiled research target, not a claimed capability.

newCandidates.name: FlashVSR
newCandidates.notes: CVPR 2026 one-step streaming VSR with locality-constrained sparse attention; official results emphasize scalability to ultra-high resolutions and efficiency. Benchmark temporal consistency and text/detail fidelity before archival use.

newCandidates.name: SparkVSR
newCandidates.notes: Interactive VSR using sparse keyframe propagation; candidate for long-video efficiency and temporal consistency. Verify the complete model-card/license stack before use.

newCandidates.name: Upscale-A-Video
newCandidates.notes: CVPR 2024 temporal-consistent diffusion VSR; useful research comparator, but license must be cleared before unrestricted production integration.

newCandidates.name: RealBasicVSR
newCandidates.notes: Real-world VSR baseline focused on restoration trade-offs; strong deterministic/reference baseline for degraded historical footage.

newCandidates.name: BasicVSR++
newCandidates.notes: Enhanced propagation and alignment; useful baseline for temporal information fusion and comparison against diffusion methods.

newCandidates.name: VRT
newCandidates.notes: Video Restoration Transformer covers video SR, deblurring, denoising, frame interpolation and space-time VSR; current official license is non-commercial, so keep outside unrestricted production unless separately cleared.

newCandidates.name: RVRT
newCandidates.notes: Recurrent video restoration transformer with guided deformable attention; strong VSR/deblurring/denoising comparator but non-commercial license requires gating.

newCandidates.name: RIFE
newCandidates.notes: Frame interpolation for motion-compensated temporal enhancement; use only to increase temporal sampling, never as evidence that spatial detail was recovered.

newCandidates.name: VideoGigaGAN
newCandidates.notes: Generative VSR research aimed at realistic detail and temporal consistency; suitable for research comparison with strict false-detail controls.

extremeResolutionStrategy.method: distributed tiled/windowed temporal restoration rather than assuming one GPU can hold the complete frame sequence
rules: Never upscale by chaining arbitrary multipliers without cross-stage validation.
Keep immutable original frames and a direct faithful restoration beside every extreme-resolution derivative.
Use overlapping tiles/windows with temporal consistency to reduce seams and flicker.
Prefer source-native evidence and multi-frame information over hallucinated texture.
A larger pixel count is not evidence of a larger recovered information content.
Any 36K/48K result must report source resolution, scale factor, compute path, model versions, seed, codec, bit depth and quality metrics.

resolutionEvidence.evidence: Official project states it can restore videos with any resolution and describes adaptive window attention for high-resolution VR; published inference guidance currently demonstrates 720p on 1x H100 and 1080p/2K on 4x H100.
Official CVPR 2026 repository states reliable scaling to ultra-high resolutions and reports 17 FPS for 768x1408 input on one A100 under its benchmark setup.

A 2026 community application advertises local 16K video output using RTX Video Super Resolution plus Real-ESRGAN restoration. This is a delivery/tooling claim, not peer-reviewed proof of faithful 16K reconstruction.

promotionRules: 36K/48K is a target output class, not a guaranteed recovered-information class.
No candidate is promoted solely because it emits a larger frame.
Temporal stability must be measured across consecutive frames and scene cuts.
For videos containing Arabic text, OCR/glyph/diacritic fidelity outranks generic perceptual scores.
Any generative model that creates plausible but unsupported detail is rejected for archival-faithful paths.
Model weights, base models, datasets and third-party components require independent rights review.
Non-commercial components remain license_gated even when their code is publicly available.
Extreme-resolution processing must preserve audio, subtitles, chapters and provenance where applicable.
No proprietary cloud service may become a core requirement merely to reach the target resolution.
